newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares dip on Saga, Norsk Hydro losses.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares dip on Saga, Norsk Hydro losses.

text.p: Norwegian shares moved into reverse on Wednesday, dragged down by steep losses in oil company Saga Petroleum and a dip from the highs by industrial giant Norsk Hydro.
The Total share index relinquished almost 0.7 percent to close at 942.71 points in heavy turnover of 1.56 billion crowns.
Most of the decline was attributed to Saga Petroleum, which resumed trading after announcing it had bought British-based Santa Fe Exploration for a bumper $1.23 billion.

Weeks of speculation, during which the price of the deal had been leaked, had left analysts downbeat on the premium Saga would pay over general estimates of Santa Fe's value which were closer to $700 to $800 million.

Saga's A share dropped nine crowns to a low at 96.50 crowns once trading resumed but came back to end five crowns off at 100.50 crowns. The B share finished 3.50 crowns off at 93.50 crowns after hitting a low at 88 crowns.
Saga accounted for 411 million crowns of total business.
Norsk Hydro also was heavily traded at a tunover of 131 million crowns and closed down two crowns at 331 crowns.
